source_text:
Ἐπὶ δὲ σοῦ, δέσποτα πανευσεβέστατε βασιλεῦ, προγονικὴν εὐσέβειαν
μείζονι τῇ πρὸς τὸ θεῖον εὐλαβείᾳ νικῶντος, οὐκ ἀπὸ γῆς λοιπόν, ἀλλ' ἐξ οὐρανῶν τὰ θαυματουργήματα· καὶ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θανάτου νικῆς τρόπαιον, ὁ μακάριος λέγω σταυρός, φωτὸς μαρμαρυγαῖς ἀπαστράπτων ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ὤφθη. 4 Ἐν γὰρ ταῖς ἁγίαις ἡμέραις ταύταις τῆς ἁγίας πεντηκοστῆς, νόνναις μαΐαις, περὶ τρίτην ὥραν, παμμεγέθης ὁ σταυρός, ἐκ φωτὸς κατεσκευασμένος, ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὑπεράνω τοῦ ἁγίου Γολγοθᾶ μέχρι τοῦ ἁγίου Ὄρους τῶν ἐλαιῶν ἐκτεταμένος ἐφαίνετο· οὐχ ἑνὶ καὶ δευτέρῳ μόνον φανείς, ἀλλὰ παντὶ τῷ τῆς πόλεως πλήθει φανερώτατα δειχθείς· οὐδ' ὡς ἄν τις νομίσειεν ὀξέως κατὰ φαντασίαν παραδραμών, ἀλλ' ἐπὶ πλείοσιν ὥραις ὑπὲρ γῆν ὀφθαλμοφανῶς θεωρούμενος, καὶ ταῖς ἀπαστραπτούσαις μαρμαρυγαῖς τὰς ἡλιακὰς ἀκτῖνας νικήσας (ἦ γὰρ ἂν ὑπ' αὐτῶν νικώμενος ἐκαλύπτετο, εἰ μὴ δυνατωτέρας ἡλίου τοῖς ὁρῶσι παρεῖχε τὰς λαμπηδόνας)· ὡς ἅπαν μὲν ἀθρόως ἐξαυτῆς εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν συνδραμεῖν τῆς πόλεως τὸ πλῆθος, τῷ τῆς θεοπτίας φόβῳ μετ' εὐφροσύνης κατασχεθέν, νέων ἅμα καὶ πρεσβύτων ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν, καὶ πάσης ἡλικίας καὶ μέχρις αὐτῶν ἤδη τῶν κατ' οἴκους θαλαμευομένων κορῶν, ἐντοπίων τε καὶ ξένων, χριστιανῶν τε ἅμα καὶ τῶν ἀλλαχόθεν ἐπιδημούντων ἐθνικῶν· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ πάντων ὡς ἐξ ἑνὸς στόματος Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν, τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μονογενῆ, τὸν θαυματοποιὸν ἀνυμνούντων, ἔργῳ τε καὶ πείρᾳ παραλαβόντων· ὅτι χριστιανῶν τὸ δόγμα τὸ πανευσεβὲς οὐκ ἐν πειθοῖς σοφίας ἐστι λόγοις, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀποδείξει
thought_title: The cross of light appears over Jerusalem
orientation: Cyril is addressing the emperor Constantius directly, contrasting the wonders of his reign with those under his father Constantine.
pass_a_gloss: But in your time, most pious master king, surpassing ancestral piety with greater reverence toward the divine, no longer from earth, but from the heavens, the wonders; and of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, the trophy of victory over death, I mean the blessed cross, flashing with gleams of light, was seen in Jerusalem. For in these holy days of holy Pentecost, on the Nones of May, about the third hour, a huge cross, made of light, in the sky, stretched above holy Golgotha as far as the holy Mount of Olives, was visible; not appearing to one and a second only, but shown most clearly to the whole multitude of the city; nor as one might suppose passing quickly by in appearance, but for more hours above the earth being seen with the eyes, and with its flashing gleams surpassing the sun's rays (for it would have been hidden, being overcome by them, if it had not provided to the beholders beams stronger than the sun); so that the whole multitude of the city at once ran together into the holy church, seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy, young and old, men and women, and of every age, and even to the very maidens shut up in their houses, locals and strangers, Christians and also the pagans visiting from elsewhere; and with one accord all, as from one mouth, hymning Christ Jesus our Lord, the only Son of God, the wonder-worker, having received in deed and experience that the most pious doctrine of Christians is not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration

choices.why: Keeps the superlative force of πανευσεβέστατε and the address δέσποτα as 'master' to preserve the deferential tone.

choices.term: τὸ κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θανάτου νικῆς τρόπαιον
choices.english: the trophy of victory over death
choices.why: Renders τρόπαιον as 'trophy' per glossary and keeps the genitive chain explicit: the trophy of the victory over death.
rejected: the sign of victory against death
the standard of triumph over death

choices.why: Preserves the participle's active flashing sense and the dative of means 'with gleams of light'.

choices.term: οὐχ ἑνὶ καὶ δευτέρῳ μόνον φανείς
choices.english: not appearing to one and a second only
choices.why: Keeps the distributive sense of 'one and a second' rather than smoothing to 'one or two', preserving the source's idiom.
rejected: not shown to just one or two
not appearing to only a few

choices.term: τῷ τῆς θεοπτίας φόβῳ μετ' εὐφροσύνης κατασχεθέν
choices.english: seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy
choices.why: Uses glossary 'heavenly vision' for θεοπτία and keeps the paired emotions of fear and joy explicit.
rejected: gripped by awe at the divine sight and joy
overcome with fear of the vision along with gladness

choices.english: is not in persuasive words of wisdom
choices.why: Echoes 1 Corinthians 2:4 wording closely while keeping the source's exact phrase structure.

pass_b_english: But in your time, most pious master king, you surpass your ancestors' piety with still greater reverence toward the divine, and the wonders come no longer from earth but from the heavens. The trophy of victory over death of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the only Son of God—I mean the blessed cross—was seen in Jerusalem, flashing with gleams of light. For during these holy days of holy Pentecost, on the Nones of May, around the third hour, a huge cross made of light appeared in the sky, stretched above holy Golgotha as far as the holy Mount of Olives. It did not appear to one and a second only, but was shown most clearly to the whole multitude of the city. Nor did it pass quickly by as one might suppose in a fleeting vision, but for many hours it was seen with the eyes above the earth, and its flashing gleams surpassed the rays of the sun—for the sun would have been overcome and hidden by them, had the cross not offered beams stronger than the sun to those who saw it. So the whole multitude of the city at once ran together into the holy church, seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy—young and old, men and women, people of every age, even young women shut up in their rooms, locals and strangers, Christians and pagans visiting from elsewhere alike. With one accord, as from a single mouth, they all sang hymns to Christ Jesus our Lord, the only Son of God, the wonderworker, having learned by deed and experience that the most pious teaching of Christians rests not in persuasive words of wisdom but in demonstration

last_rejected.quote: The trophy of victory over death
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θανάτου νικῆς τρόπαιον
last_rejected.why: Greek is 'the trophy against the victory of death' or 'the trophy of victory over death'—κατὰ + genitive here means 'against' or 'over' in sense of triumphing over. 'Trophy of victory over death' captures this well. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek phrase means trophy of victory over death, translation matches

last_rejected.why: Greek word order is 'the blessed, I say, cross'—English 'I mean the blessed cross' is natural. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘ὁ μακάριος λέγω σταυρός’ rendered naturally as ‘I mean the blessed cross’

last_rejected.why: νόνναις = Nones (Roman calendar date), μαΐαις = of May. Correct.

last_rejected.ruling: περὶ τρίτην ὥραν = about the third hour

last_rejected.source_quote: παμμεγέθης ὁ σταυρός, ἐκ φωτὸς κατεσκευασμένος
last_rejected.ruling: παμμεγέθης… ἐκ φωτὸς κατεσκευασμένος = huge cross made of light

last_rejected.quote: stretched above holy Golgotha as far as the holy Mount of Olives
last_rejected.source_quote: ὑπεράνω τοῦ ἁγίου Γολγοθᾶ μέχρι τοῦ ἁγίου Ὄρους τῶν ἐλαιῶν ἐκτεταμένος
last_rejected.why: Correct—stretched above Golgotha as far as the Mount of Olives.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπέρ α τοῦ ἁγίου Γολγοθᾶ … ἕως τοῦ ἁγίου Ὄρους τῶν ἐλαιῶν = stretched above Golgotha to Mount of Olives

last_rejected.quote: to one and a second only
last_rejected.why: Correct—not to one and a second only.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐχ ἑνὶ καὶ δευτέρῳ μόνον = not to one and a second only

last_rejected.quote: for many hours it was seen with the eyes above the earth
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐπὶ πλείοσιν ὥραις ὑπὲρ γῆν ὀφθαλμοφανῶς θεωρούμενος
last_rejected.why: Correct—for many hours, above the earth, visibly (with eyes) being seen.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπὶ πλείοσιν ὥραις … ὑπὲρ γῆν ὀφθαλμοφανῶς θεωρούμενος = seen for many hours above earth

last_rejected.why: ἐθνικῶν = gentiles/pagans, ἀλλαχόθεν ἐπιδημούντων = visiting from elsewhere. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: τῶν ἀλλαχόθεν ἐπιδημούντων ἐθνικῶν = gentiles/pagans visiting from elsewhere

last_rejected.quote: seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ τῆς θεοπτίας φόβῳ μετ' εὐφροσύνης κατασχεθέν
last_rejected.why: Checking—English has 'seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy' which captures τῷ τῆς θεοπτίας φόβῳ μετ' εὐφροσύνης κατασχεθέν. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: τῷ τῆς θεοπτίας φόβῳ μετ' εὐφροσύνης κατασχεθέν = seized with fear of the heavenly vision together with joy

last_rejected.why: English has 'into the holy church.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν = into the holy church
ἐντοπίων τε καὶ ξένων = locals and strangers

last_rejected.quote: with one accord, as from a single mouth
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ πάντων ὡς ἐξ ἑνὸς στόματος
last_rejected.why: English has 'With one accord, as from a single mouth.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁμοθυμαδὸν … ὡς ἐξ ἑνὸς στόματος = with one accord, as from a single mouth

last_rejected.why: Greek 'flashing with gleams of light.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: φωτὸς μαρμαρυγαῖς ἀπαστράπτων = flashing with gleams of light

last_rejected.quote: So the whole multitude of the city at once ran together
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς ἅπαν μὲν ἀθρόως ἐξαυτῆς εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν συνδραμεῖν τῆς πόλεως τὸ πλῆθος
last_rejected.why: Greek 'so that the whole multitude of the city at once ran together into the holy church.' English 'So the whole multitude of the city at once ran together'—wait, English omits 'into the holy church' at this point? Let me check: English says 'So the whole multitude of the city at once ran together into the holy church'—yes, it's there. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: συνδραμεῖν … = ran together, translation includes this

last_rejected.quote: even young women shut up in their rooms
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μέχρις αὐτῶν ἤδη τῶν κατ' οἴκους θαλαμευομένων κορῶν
last_rejected.why: English adds a specific group (young women) not present in Greek; Greek mentions all house‑bound persons.
last_rejected.fix: even those already confined to their houses
last_rejected.ruling: κορῶν means 'maidens/young women'; θαλαμευομένων means 'chambered/shut in rooms'—translation accurate.

last_rejected.quote: young and old, men and women, people of every age,
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μέχρις αὐτῶν ἤδη τῶν κατ' οἴκους θαλαμευομένων κορῶν
last_rejected.why: The phrase about all house‑bound people is omitted, narrowing the description.
last_rejected.fix: young and old, men and women, people of every age, and even those already confined to their houses
last_rejected.ruling: The house-bound maidens are rendered; not omitted. 'even young women shut up in their rooms' translates the phrase.
